QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_5

question.text: In the context of Dharma Private Equity Fund, a Category II AIF, the 'Hurdle Rate' means:

answer.text: The minimum return the manager guarantees investors
The minimum accrued rate of return below which the manager earns NO incentive fees
The maximum leverage the fund can take
The expense cap agreed with LPs

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.2: The Hurdle Rate (also called the preferred return) is the minimum rate of return that must accrue to investors before the manager becomes entitled to any incentive/carried-interest fees. It defines the profit-split threshold in the waterfall, not a guaranteed return. The Trap: Option A is wrong because the hurdle is a profit-split threshold, not a guarantee — AIFs do not guarantee returns. Option C confuses the hurdle with leverage limits, and Option D conflates it with an expense cap, which is a separate negotiation point. Note: Incentive fees apply only on returns above the hurdle; the hurdle itself does not promise that investors will earn that minimum return.
